title: Predict: Serial Queue Ordering
hints: A serial queue runs blocks one at a time in the order they were enqueued.
`sync` doesn't return until its block — and everything queued before it — has run.
jsBridge: A serial queue runs blocks one at a time in FIFO order. `async` enqueues and returns, and `sync` enqueues and waits. JS's event loop is one serial queue, so the ordering intuition carries over, but `sync` has no JS equivalent.

compass.q: `setTimeout(f, 0)` is like `queue.async`. What would a blocking `queue.sync` mean on JS's single thread?
`queue.sync` from inside a block already running on `queue`: why does it deadlock?
Serial vs concurrent queues: which gives ordering guarantees?
`DispatchQueue.main.async` vs `@MainActor`: which should new code use?
